The Brushworn Standard

If it hasn't been carried, soaked, frozen, or bled on by us, it isn't Brushworn.

A lot of what can go wrong is preventable and predictable. Heat, cold, busted boot leather, cut pads, cheatgrass awns, icy water, leaky waders, a long drive out of the woods. None of it is in the manual that came with your dog or your gear.

Brushworn is built to fill that gap: field health for dogs that work in the most punishing conditions, and the gear that keeps your trip or training running smoothly. Categories will come and go. The standard remains.

In the works

What's coming from Brushworn

Kits, protocol cards, and a short list of gear for the trips & training that ask the most of a dog.

  • Field kits

    Season and trip-specific dog first aid

    Not just a generic bag. Kits assembled for the conditions you're actually in (or headed to). Heat, late-season cold water, prairie or western scree, all with contents chosen alongside a sporting dog veterinarian.

  • Protocol cards

    What to do, and the order to do it in

    A waterproof card in every kit, keyed to that kit's contents and laid out for cold, shaking hands. Includes the triggers that indicate it's time to stop and drive to a vet now, and the info that will help you get your dog there safely.

  • Refills

    Restocked before it expires

    Supplies age out and get used up. We'll tell you when yours are due so you don't have to keep track, and make replacing them easy so you're always prepared.

  • Curated gear

    Short lists, lots of miles

    Kennels, carry, water, warmth, recovery. A tight user-curated selection from other makers, added one piece at a time as the gear earns its place.

Who's behind it

Built by people who run dogs.

Most of what we know about keeping a dog going, we learned from the dogs. Grouse and woodcock cover in Maine, prairie grass out west, blood-tracking deer on oak ridges, and more cold mornings on salt water than we can count.

In addition to hunting, I judge NAVHDA tests, which means a lot of days watching other people's dogs work and noticing what goes wrong in the field, be it with the dog or gear.

The medical side comes from Charles Ellithorpe, DVM, a sporting dog veterinarian (and former western big game nut) who hunts hard behind his own dogs in the same kinds of cover. He co-authors our field guides and helps to build and provision our field kits. Nothing clinical goes out without his eyes on it.

Brushworn exists because the answers that matter on a hard day, and the gear that gets you through them, are scattered across forum threads, phone calls, and mistakes you only make once. We'd rather they were in one place.

See you in the woods.
PJ & Charles
